title: Basic Structure doctrine
quote: Parliament may amend any part under Art. 368 - but cannot alter, damage or destroy its core features

boxes.title: Meaning & origin
items: ==**Judge-made**==, nowhere defined; not by any Act (APPSC-G1 2024)
Idea from **Germany** (Basic Law); jurist **Dietrich Conrad** (1965): implied limits
Justice **Mudholkar** (Sajjan Singh dissent) first said "basic features"
List **never exhaustively defined**; grows case by case

items.what: ==**Kesavananda Bharati**==: **13 judges**, **7:6**, CJI **S.M. Sikri**; doctrine propounded
**Indira Gandhi v. Raj Narain**: first application; **39th** clause struck

boxes.title: Elements → case
head: Element
Case
rows: **Free and fair elections**, rule of law
Judicial review, limited amending power, FR-DPSP harmony

boxes.title: Ninth Schedule story
steps: **1st Amendment (1951)**: Art. **31B** + Ninth Schedule for land reforms
Entries only by Parliament via amendment (e.g. **76th, 1994**: TN **69%**)

boxes.title: Supremacy & debate
items: Judicial review → ==supremacy of Constitution and courts== (APPSC-G2 2017)
Indian Parliament **not sovereign** in British sense
HCs can void central laws: 42nd bar removed by **43rd (1977)**
Criticism: no textual basis, open-ended; defence: shield against majorities
**129th Bill**: **B.R. Gavai** - no violation; **U.U. Lalit, Sanjiv Khanna** - doubts

boxes.title: Exam corner
items: False: "defined in **Part XX**"; "FRs can never be amended"
Core features cannot be altered by Parliament (APPSC-GS 2024)
